title: session-longtail-attn-oddball-notes
content:
Goal: capture repro, commands, fast hypotheses for the long-tail session bug where KV indexes slip and attention kernel selection flips mid-session.

Background/context:
- Happening intermittently on dev-dedicated nodes and sometimes in local repro when we use mixed-length requests in same session.
- Symptoms: model output starts correct, then after ~10–50 consecutive requests with varied sequence lengths, later responses contain unexpected attention decay to early tokens (like prefixes) or outright token hallucination. KV cache inspection shows offset inconsistencies (keys for recent tokens appear at older slot indexes).
- Not typical eviction: total KV size is under configured max. Seems like index rollover / pointer arithmetic glitch when a request with extremely large seqlen appears (>= 65k-ish in synthetic). Real traffic uses 8–4096, but combined prefix/prompt+completion can create effective seqlen > 8192 in some tests.

Repro (fast script):
- harness: tests/longtail_repro.sh (local) — uses local runtime binary built from HEAD. Steps below are minimal reproduce sequence.

Minimal repro steps (local build):
1) export ENV for deterministic kernels:
   export REDWOOD_DEBUG_FORCE_KERNEL=auto
   export REDWOOD_KV_WRAP_PANIC=1  # trigger panic on wrap (dev only)
2) start runtime with trace flags:
   ./redwood-runtime --config configs/dev-dedicated.toml \
     --trace-level debug --trace-output /tmp/rt-trace.log &
3) run requests: (python small script)
   - send 8 requests with seqlen 512 (prompt 256 + completion 256)
   - then 1 request with seqlen ~8192 (prompt 7700 + completion 512)
   - then 20 requests with seqlen 128
Expected: later small requests should continue normal. Observed: after big-seq request, subsequent responses sometimes use stale KV entries.

Logs and snippets (grep-able):
- /tmp/rt-trace.log lines around the incident:
  [2026-02-18T14:03:22Z] KVCache::insert key_idx=32767 logical_pos=32767 real_pos=65535
  [2026-02-18T14:03:22Z] KVCache::wrap detected wrap_at=65536 new_base=65536
  [2026-02-18T14:03:22Z] AttentionKernel::select selected=flashfwd fallback=flash_attn_v2 reason=seqlenChange threshold=4096
  [2026-02-18T14:03:22Z] KVCache::resolve requested_pos=65538 resolved_to=2  # suspicious small index mapping
  [2026-02-18T14:03:22Z] Response::trace attention_mask_applied_start=0 attention_mask_applied_end=128

Error/stack excerpt (from local panic with REDWOOD_KV_WRAP_PANIC=1):
  panic: kv index overflow: requested 65538 > capacity 65536
  goroutine 34 [running]:
  runtime/debug.Stack(0x0, 0x0, 0x0)
      /usr/local/go/src/runtime/debug/stack.go:24 +0x9f
  redwood/serving/kv.(*Cache).Resolve(0xc000104000, 0x10002, 0x0)
      /home/maya/code/redwood/serving/kv/cache.go:213 +0x1a4
  redwood/serving/attention.(*Planner).Plan(0xc00011f000, 0xc0000b4000, 0x2d)
      /home/maya/code/redwood/serving/attention/planner.go:89 +0x2b0

What we've tried (experiments and quick notes):
- Hypothesis A: sign/overflow in kv base index arithmetic when base increases by power-of-two thresholds.
  - Added assertions around base increment (PR local/patch: GH#4917). Repro still occurs (assertions not firing because wrap logic sets base then resolves mapping incorrectly).
- Hypothesis B: attention kernel selection path mutates global seqlen state or uses stale per-session metadata; kernel switch triggers different KV addressing semantics (flashfwd expects continuous addressing, flash_attn_v2 uses relative offsets).
  - Forced kernel to flash_attn_v2 only via REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn_v2 — repro disappears.
  - Forced kernel to flashfwd — repro becomes more deterministic and faster to trigger.
- Hypothesis C: per-request KV compression/compaction routine runs asynchronously and races with insert; rare race causes real_pos update to be one step behind, then kernel selection computes spans using stale base.
  - Added mutex around compaction in local branch. Repro rate reduced but not eliminated. Suggests race is one contributor.
- Hypothesis D: sequence length estimator in routing layer clamps incorrectly for very long prompt, causing planner to choose kernel that can't handle the effective position space.
  - Added extra logging in routing estimator; saw mismatches in seqlen reported to planner vs actually used by runtime.

Data points and metrics to collect next run:
- KV metrics per-request: insert_count, compaction_count, base_before, base_after, requested_pos, resolved_pos (emit as trace).
- Kernel selection sample: requested_seq_len, chosen_kernel, kernel_thresholds, kernel_version
- Traces for per-session metadata (session_id -> last_seq_len -> kernel_used_history)

Immediate actionable steps (short-term):
1) Add defensive mapping check: when Resolve maps requested_pos -> resolved_to, if requested_pos - resolved_to > 65536/2 then log full mapping and dump last 100 inserts for session. (low-risk instrumentation)
2) Run overnight fuzz harness with 1M mixed requests across 6 local nodes, vary long-seq bursts and include kernel forcing permutations to measure correlation. (testbed: qa-fuzz-6)
3) Build variant that disables async compaction (make compaction stop-the-world) to see elimination rate; if repro goes away, we know race ordering is core.
4) For immediate mitigation in prod: add server flag that disables largest-kernel selector (prevent flashfwd selection for sessions that exceed cumulative tokens > 64k). Use circuit-breaker rollout.

Longer-term/architectural thoughts:
- Kernel semantic contract: we currently assume kernels are interchangeable given same token indexing semantics. We should formalize kernel capabilities: addressing model (absolute vs relative), max-address-space, wrap semantics. Store kernel capability descriptors and verify at selection time.
- KV addressing should be versioned: any change to base arithmetic must increment KV schema version per runtime; old sessions either be forced to compatible kernel/mapper or be migrated.

Hypothesis ranking (quick):
1) Kernel/mapper semantic mismatch after wrap (most likely)
2) Async compaction race (medium)
3) Unexpected seqlen estimator mismatch (low-medium)
4) Memory allocator aliasing causing overwritten entries (low)

Quick checklist for next debug session:
- [ ] Run fuzz harness with REDWOOD_DEBUG_DUMP_KV=1 for 24h and collect samples.
- [ ] Push instrumented Resolve logging (GH#4933).
- [ ] Try stop-the-world compaction (branch: stop-compaction-dev).
- [ ] Prepare rollback flag to force kernel=flash_attn_v2 in prod (feature flag: kernel-fallback-force-v2).

Notes-to-self / loose breadcrumbs:
- The weird resolved_to small index (2) after wrap looked like modulo arithmetic. Maybe there is a missing +base or -base in one of the mapper functions. Search keywords: "resolvePos", "mapToReal", "kv_base_offset" in repo.
- Check commit history around cache.go:213 for any refactors touching indexing (author: R. Patel, commit 2025-10-15).
- When kernel selection flips, check if planner.Plan mutates session.state.seqlen_hint. If so, it's a bad side-effect.

Experimental flags tried (summary):
- REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn_v2 -> repro stops
- REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=flashfwd -> repro highly reproducible
- REDWOOD_KV_WRAP_PANIC=1 -> produced goroutine stack above
- REDWOOD_KV_ASYNC_COMPACT=0 -> repro rate ~3x lower

Appendix: small helper to dump kv state (quick python):
- /scripts/dump_kv_state.py (connects to runtime debug socket and prints last N entries with logical/real mapping)

Next owners and quick comms:
- Owner (investigation): Maya Chen (me)
- Pairing: Liam O'Neill (attention kernels) for kernel contract review
- Notify if you flip any runtime flags in staging: ping #eng-runtime with tag [kv-longtail]

If you pick this up mid-week: start with forcing kernel->v2 and run the 1-hour mixed harness; compare KV mapping traces for failures vs success.

End of notes.
